I have finally decided, that today I will move over to Linux. After a long time, looking at and testing the various distros, my decision is to use Debian. Today I will finally be making the transition to Linux

I'd really recommend going with something a bit more user-friendly. Don't get me wrong, Debian is a great distro and is fairly user-friendly, but if you're getting your toes wet, maybe you should go with Linux Mint. It is Ubuntu/Debian-based, which means it has all of the advantages of using Debian, but it also is easier to use.

However, if you don't want to go straight Mint, and want your Debian, then there's this: http://www.linuxmint.com/download_lmde.php (Linux Mint Debian Edition)

It was originally between Debian and Mint. I had read that mint is basically just a nicer desktop environment, and has a smaller package list and was worried that some tools i needed may not be released on Mint. I should also mention that I intend to learn some of the availabe digital forensic tools.Although I am considering dual boot with Deft for that.

That LMDE looks interesting, thanks for that... will now have another read!

Linux Mint has a larger package list than it lets on. It was originally based on Ubuntu, so any Ubuntu packages, Debian Packages, or Mint packages work. There's a quick-n-easy way to get Kali's offensive security tools for Linux Mint as well.

Debian is also more focused on free software, so you may have to add some extra repos if you want proprietary things. Mint comes with more support for non-free stuff out of the box. That said, you can do anything with any system, it's just easier to start with something close to what you want imho.

Just wanted to chime in that I switched to Linux Mint cinnamon edition and I'm a "stupid windows user". So far I have done things I never really though possible.

Steam Linux works great for linux games. I use PlayOnLinux which is a WINE GUI for gaming. I installed Steam Windows and installed my windows game and I just play like normal.
I second the consideration of Mint. I recently switched from Ubuntu Gnome (I don't care for Unity) to Mint, much nicer, easier to use for daily stuff.

After listening to the various comments, I will give the LMDE a try. Mint seems to be getting the most recommendations, however as I would like to challenge myself and learn the nitty gritty configurations, Debian seems to be the way forward. So as suggested that Mint Debian is the best of both worlds, I will give it a go. Thanks for the input everyone.

Honestly, if you really want to challenge yourself you can always download source code and compile it specifically for your system. A .deb package will run on mint because its built ontop of Debian/Ubuntu. All a package is (think .deb, or .rpm) is a precompiled program, that was compiled specifically for a target system. There's also programs like alien which will take one systems package and recompile it for another.

Debian..A man after my own heart.. Debian (stable) is my primary OS, has been for years. It's like installing a blank canvass that you can paint something on that's truly your own. I use the KDE Plasma Desktop, it's simply wonderful. Infinitely customizable.

I have LMDE installed on another drive and that's also a possible alternative, I like it, very crisp and stable,..but not as a primary OS. ;-)
